did_you_know.text: Did you know? Psalm 111 is a psalm of thanksgiving. At its opening, the speaker declares that he gives thanks to the Lord with all his heart, among the upright and in the congregation.
Did you know? The psalm describes the Lord’s works as great and worthy of study and reflection, emphasizing the importance of contemplating them.
Did you know? According to the verse, the Lord’s work is characterized by majesty and splendor, and his righteousness endures forever.
Did you know? The verse connects the Lord’s wonders with an enduring remembrance and describes him as gracious and compassionate.
Did you know? The Lord is described as providing food for those who fear him and remembering his covenant forever.
Did you know? The psalm states that the Lord reveals the power of his works to his people, including the giving of the nations’ inheritance.
Did you know? The works of the Lord’s hands are described as truth and justice, and his precepts as trustworthy.
Did you know? The verse emphasizes that the Lord’s works and precepts stand firm forever and are carried out in truth and uprightness.
Did you know? The psalm brings together the sending of redemption to his people, the keeping of his covenant, and the description of the Lord’s name as holy and awesome.

Did you know? The psalm presents the fear of the Lord as the beginning of wisdom and sound understanding as the gift of those who keep his commandments. It is also arranged as an alphabetical acrostic, from the beginning of the alphabet to its end.
